newsitem.title: UK: UK house prices rise 0.5 pct in August - Halifax.
newsitem.headline: UK house prices rise 0.5 pct in August - Halifax.

text.p: UK house prices rose by a seasonally adjusted 0.5 percent in August, the same as in July, according to the Halifax Building Society's latest house price index. The annual rate of house price inflation is now 5.7 percent, up from 5.3 in July, the Halifax said.
That leaves overall house prices 5.6 percent above the early 1993 trough but 8.1 percent below the peak in 1989.
"The further small rise this month confirms our view that house prices are now steadily recovering," a Halifax statement said.

But given the rise in house prices seen in the second half of last year it said: "We would expect the annual rate of (house price) inflation to remain broadly stable at around five percent over the next few months."
In 1997, it said annual prices rises of five to seven percent were expected.
Prices paid by first time buyers jumped 0.7 percent in August, taking the annual rate up to 5.9 percent. The average price paid by a first time buyer was 47,482 stg, the Halifax said.
Conversely, prices of new houses fell for the second successive month in August, dropping 0.4 percent. The average price of a new house was 69,407 stg.
